title: compact-action-velocity-scrapbook
content:
Purpose: a compact, repeatable two-week scrapbook to test tiny, measurable behaviors that should move my personal KPIs (focus hours, PR throughput, bug debt) while keeping it low overhead. Use this as: a quick check-in before Friday, a short retrospective after the two-week window, and a lightweight experiment log.

Right-now thesis (why this matters): small, consistent bursts of focused work + deliberate handoffs increase PR completion rate and reduce rework. If I can reliably convert 3 small PRs/week into merged changes with <1 follow-up comment each, the product velocity metric should move and reduce stress.

Two-week goals (hypothesis-driven):
- H1 (focus): 8x 60-minute deep blocks (total 8 hours/week) scheduled and protected — measured as calendar events + toggled Do Not Disturb.
- H2 (throughput): Merge 6 small PRs (<= 200 LOC) with median time-to-merge <72 hours.
- H3 (quality): Keep post-merge bug fixes related to these PRs <= 2 across the window.

Mini-metrics (tracking table, recorded daily):
- Day | Deep blocks completed | PRs opened | PRs merged | Followups on merged PRs | Notes
- Mon | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | started refactor A (blocked by infra)
- Tue | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | finished small docs PR
- Wed | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | review back-and-forth on feature B
- Thu | 2 | 0 | 1 | 0 | pair with Ava for acceptance tests
- Fri | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | queued an experiment toggle
(keep updating; this is an excerpt — full daily rows in my calendar notes)

Micro-experiments (active):
- E1: "No meetings before 11" on Mon/Tue/Wed to force two morning deep blocks. (status: partial success; Mon/Wed good, Tue slipped due to ad-hoc incident)
- E2: Pre-PR checklist: 5 manual checks (unit test, lint, README entry, simple smoke run, change log entry) before draft. (status: good — reduced review churn)
- E3: Pair-review handoff: schedule 20-min sync instead of full comments for complex PRs. (status: promising; saved ~30m of review cycles)

Retrospective notes (end of two-week window):
- Wins: pre-PR checklist eliminated one round of nit comments on average. Pair-review handoffs felt higher ROI than long threads. Protected deep blocks correlate with faster merges on days I keep them.
- Misses: unplanned infra incidents still kill morning blocks; need a fallback slot in afternoon. PR size creep — some PRs drifted >200 LOC and took longer.
- Unexpected: documenting the tiny checklist made my reviewers more confident to merge without gating input.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Should I set a hard PR size limit (e.g., 200 LOC) and split anything larger into a two-step change? Pros: faster merges. Cons: potential coordination overhead.
- How to handle recurring infra interruptions? Option A: reserve a daily 40-min 'rescue' block; Option B: carve out two afternoons/week for ad-hoc.
- Do I make the pre-PR checklist a templated file in the repo to encourage adoption? (linked to RG-4021)

Immediate next steps (next two weeks):
- Action 1: Enforce 1 deep-block before any PR draft (even 30 mins) — trial for 2 weeks.
- Action 2: Add a PR template with the 5 quick checks (create a one-line checklist file). Owner: me. ETA: this week.
- Action 3: Experiment placing one 'rescue' block at 4pm Tue/Thu. Reassess after 2 weeks.

Notes-to-self (short heuristics I want to remember):
- Small PRs beat perfect PRs.
- Visibility beats assumptions: ping once to confirm deployment windows.
- Pairing early saves 3x in review time later.

Scratch items / todo: (two-minute brain dump)
- Draft PR template -> open RG-4021
- Slack note to Ava about pairing cadence
- Move recurring "deep-block" to calendar as 'focus: do-not-disturb' and add color
- Run a quick post-merge smoke test script (add to repo scripts)

Quick status log (last update): 2026-03-11: mid-cycle check: 4/8 deep blocks done this week, 3 PRs merged, one PR needs follow-up from infra.

Permissions note: personal scratchpad. I share this with Mikael and Ava for quick feedback and pair scheduling. If something is actionable to the team, move it to RG-4021 / JIRA-1287.

Reflection prompt for next edit (two weeks): Did the rescue block reduce morning interruptions? Did pre-PR checklist continue to reduce review cycles? If not, iterate on one change only — either rescue block or PR template.
